oil.summary: Crude booked a strong week — Brent +4.48%, WTI +4.04% — anchored squarely in Hormuz risk premium as the US-Iran conflict grinds on with no diplomatic resolution in sight. Tanker crossings through the strait slumped to as few as five in a single day this week, and three vessels were reported damaged in the Gulf, keeping physical supply anxiety elevated. Houthi drone attacks on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery added a second front of disruption. Headline crude gains were, however, undercut at the product level: RBOB gasoline cratered 8.78% on the session and is down 13.13% on the month, consistent with VP Vance's declaration that cheap pump prices are Washington's "goal number one." Heating oil shed 3.30% on the day despite a solid weekly gain. Asian refiners are pivoting to US crude as Hormuz access deteriorates, while Russia quietly captured a record 50%-plus share of India's import market.
drivers: Hormuz gridlock: tanker crossings at multi-week lows, three vessels damaged, Iranian military contests US control claims
Geopolitical escalation broadening — Houthi drone strike on Aramco's Jazan refinery adds Gulf infrastructure risk
White House political pressure on gasoline prices weighing on product cracks; RBOB -8.78% on the day

gas.summary: Natural gas markets diverged sharply by geography this week. TTF surged 9.50% on the week and 11.02% on the month to 60.82 €/MWh, reflecting European anxiety over LNG supply routes through a contested Strait of Hormuz — Iranian forces have explicitly rejected US claims of control over the waterway, raising the spectre of prolonged transit disruption. Henry Hub is a far quieter story: the front month edged up 1.61% today to $2.771/MMBtu and is +4.09% on the week, but remains 3.04% below month-ago levels, suggesting domestic fundamentals are still soft. The Vance "goal number one" framing on energy prices adds a policy overlay, though headline news on US gas-specific fundamentals is thin today.
drivers: Hormuz LNG supply risk driving outsized TTF rally — +9.50% on the week vs Henry Hub's modest +4.09%
Iranian military's rejection of US Hormuz control claims sustains European supply-security premium
Henry Hub subdued relative to TTF; domestic US fundamentals remain soft with month-on-month price still negative

power.summary: The power and carbon complex faces a convergence of structural and geopolitical pressures. EU carbon (EUA) is little-changed near-term — down 0.72% on the day and only +0.80% on the week at $77.64 — but TTF's 11% monthly surge feeds directly into gas-fired generation costs across Europe. On the demand side, US power grids are straining under what is reported to be record electricity consumption driven by Big Tech data center buildout, with demand expected to set new all-time highs both this year and next. India's coal demand trajectory adds another long-term demand signal, with projections pointing to 1.6 billion tons by 2030 versus roughly 1.2 billion today. A Trump administration push into EV minerals — despite the president's historically sceptical stance on clean energy — rounds out the picture as an emerging policy signal worth monitoring.
drivers: US power demand hitting record highs driven by data center buildout, tightening grid margins
TTF +11% month-on-month inflating European gas-fired generation costs; EUA pricing not yet fully reflecting pass-through
India coal demand forecast to rise 33% to 1.6 bn tons by 2030; Trump EV-minerals spending signals a nuanced clean-energy policy shift
